Notes:
The Board suspended the rules of procedure to move the following motion:
MOTION OPL 20260512/1
Moved by Vice-Chair Kathy Fisher:
WHEREAS the 2026 Board meeting schedule was approved by the Board on October 14, 2025 (OPLB-2025-1014-10.4); and,
WHEREAS from time to time, staff may be required to adjust the Board meeting schedule due to circumstances not foreseen at the time of approval; and,
WHEREAS the next Ādisōke project update report to the Board is anticipated in June 2026, as noted in the December 2025 update to the Board; and,
WHEREAS project construction updates are also provided to the City of Ottawa Finance and Corporate Services Committee by the project management office within the City's Infrastructure and Water Services; and,
WHEREAS the above-mentioned update is anticipated at the June 2, 2026 Finance and Corporate Services Committee meeting; 
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT RESOLVED THAT the Ottawa Public Library Board meeting date of Tuesday, June 9, 2026 at 5:00pm be rescheduled to Tuesday, June 2, 2026 at 5:00pm, in order to align with the timing of the Finance and Corporate Services Committee meeting.
Results: Carried

agenda_items.title: Chair's Verbal Update
agenda_items.minutes:
Intellectual Freedom Advocacy
Chair Luloff commended the Board for its strong stance on intellectual freedom, noting that it maintains one of North America’s most robust position statements to ensure open access to information and support inquiry. He emphasized that this commitment informs both governance and OPL services, referenced the February 2026 Freedom to Read Week activities, and indicated that a motion reaffirming the Board’s position will be considered in response to emerging challenges later in this evening’s meeting.
City of Ottawa’s Access-Ability Day 2026
Chair Luloff highlighted the City of Ottawa’s upcoming Access‑Ability Day and the alignment of this year’s theme “Game Changers,” with OPL’s commitment to reducing barriers to participation. He added that OPL will host a booth highlighting accessible services that support learning, wellness, and community connection.
MOTION OPL 20260512/2
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chair’s verbal update for information.
Results: Received

agenda_items.title: Chief Executive Officer / Chief Librarian’s Report
agenda_items.minutes:
Historic Day at Main Branch
Sonia Bebbington, Chief Executive Officer and Chief Librarian, reported that the Horwood Window has been temporarily removed from the Main Branch for restoration and preparation for installation at the Central branch at Ādisōke. Created by early Canadian stained-glass artist Henry Horwood, the window will be cleaned and refurbished with support from the Friends of the Public Library Association (FOPLA), who are also contributing to its relocation. Originally part of the historic Carnegie building, the window features notable writers and poets, including Ottawa’s Archibald Lampman. Once restored, it will be displayed in a new light-filled setting. Harvey A. Slack recalled discussions during his first term as a Board member, also including interest from former member Allan Higdon, about incorporating historically significant items into the new facility, and expressed delight at this news and commended staff.
Upcoming Closure
Ms. Bebbington announced that OPL branches will be closed on May 18 for Victoria Day, and highlighted OPL’s online services at BiblioOttawaLibrary.ca.
MOTION OPL 20260512/3
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chief Librarian/CEO’s report for information.
Results: Received

sub_agendas_items.title: OPL Board Commitment to Intellectual Freedom and Support for National Association Advocacy - Motion (Chair Matthew Luloff)
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Chair Luloff emphasized that public libraries are vital democratic institutions that provide equitable access to information, support privacy, and encourage independent thinking. While acknowledging the importance of caregiver involvement in decisions about children’s reading materials, he raised concerns about Alberta’s proposed Bill 28, noting the bill would allow increased government oversight of libraries, including the ability to inspect materials, compel information from staff, and regulate access to materials by age, shifting control away from local library boards and professional librarians. Chair Luloff cautioned that this risks government interference and is a departure from established Canadian library principles, which prioritize professional standards, local accountability, and public trust over political control. He said the motion highlights the challenges to intellectual freedom that are occurring across various regions, underlining the importance of national unity among library organizations. Lastly, he underlined that the motion reaffirms the Board’s commitment to intellectual freedom, and signals support for advocacy statements from Canadian library organizations of which OPL is a member. In closing, Chair Luloff said he supports balancing protecting children and the rights of parents to be involved in what their children read with the defense of intellectual freedom, privacy, and the independence of public libraries.
There being no further discussion, the motion was CARRIED as presented.
MOTION OPL 20260512/7
WHEREAS the Ottawa Public Library (OPL) Board has taken a strong stand in support of free and open access to information as a cornerstone to a democratic society, respecting individual rights to both privacy and choice, as reflected in OPL’s Intellectual Freedom Position Statement; and, 
WHEREAS the proposed amendments to the Alberta Libraries Act in Bill 28 represent a significant departure from long-standing Canadian public library principles, including independent, locally governed library boards and professional, evidence-based collection management, and set a concerning precedent with potential implications for public libraries across Canada; and,
WHEREAS national library associations have raised concerns that legislated restrictions on access to library materials risk undermining intellectual freedom, eroding personal privacy, and weakening public trust in libraries;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Ottawa Public Library Board reaffirm its commitment to intellectual freedom as described in the Board’s position statement; and, 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the OPL Board express its support for the statement made by the Canadian Urban Libraries Council (CULC), in turn supporting the  April 2, 2026 statement by the Coalition of Alberta Public Libraries (CAP Libraries); and,
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the OPL Board direct the CEO and Chief Librarian to communicate this resolution to the Canadian Federation of Library Associations (CFLA), the Federation of Ontario Public Libraries (FOPL), CAP Libraries, and CULC.
Results: Carried
